features.description: Wrong-worktree refusal (moved from worktree-isolation-v0 F003 at its D012 split): every plan-mutating entry point shares one fail-closed guard precondition built on v0's canonical binding_health predicate.
features.acceptance: `plan lock`, `plan audit`, `plan close`, `plan disposition`, and the orchestrate dispatch entry point share ONE guard precondition evaluated BEFORE any gate side effect or evidence write: the registry loads via the STRICT path (a corrupt registry file FAILS CLOSED with a distinct registry-corrupt error naming the file — never the unbound passthrough); when the plan has a binding, the invoking working tree (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) must equal the bound worktree_path with BOTH sides fully resolved (symlinks and relative components canonicalized via realpath-equivalent resolution) before comparison — symlinked or case-variant spellings of the same directory neither falsely refuse nor falsely pass AND the binding must pass the canonical binding_health predicate (F004 — the guard CALLS it, never re-specifies health conditions), so a deleted worktree replaced by an unrelated repository at the same path and branch refuses with the predicate's reason; any unhealthy or indeterminate state refuses fail-closed naming the failed conjunct plus the exact create/override commands; the override flag is honoured for the JUDGMENT refusal classes only — wrong invoking path, unhealthy binding (including swapped-repo and branch-drift conjuncts), and indeterminate git state — while a CORRUPT REGISTRY is NEVER overridable (infrastructure corruption must be repaired, not waived; the refusal says so and a test asserts the override flag is rejected for it); for the overridable classes the flag with a required reason proceeds ONLY AFTER the override record (plan_id, invoking path, bound path, reason, actor, timestamp) AND the binding snapshot are DURABLY written — written, flushed, AND fsynced to disk (the crash-durability contract: a process crash immediately after the guard proceeds must leave both artifacts readable) — in the plan's audit evidence — if either evidence write fails the guarded command refuses instead of proceeding un-evidenced (a combined override-path test asserts both artifacts land, and a write-failure test asserts the refusal); plans with no binding in a VALID (or absent) registry are never refused (backward-compatibility regression test); DontPanic has NO merge command — merging is the operator's external gh ritual; the guarded set above IS the complete set of PLAN-GATE commands (those that mutate plan/gate state and write gate evidence), and that scoping is an explicit decision: the worktree-MANAGEMENT commands (worktree create and worktree remove) are deliberately OUTSIDE the wrong-worktree guard — they operate on bindings by plan id from any checkout and are protected by their own preconditions (strict registry load, binding_health, cleanliness, the override-free corrupt-registry refusal) rather than by invoking-path identity (a test asserts create and remove run unguarded from the main checkout while lock/audit/close/disposition/dispatch refuse), and this feature OWNS that guard with a CLI-surface test asserting the plan command namespace exposes no merge subcommand; tests cover refusal per guarded entry point, each binding_health conjunct refusal through the guard, corrupt-registry refusal AND its override rejection, override-with-reason recording plus snapshot capture for each overridable class, and the unbound passthrough. all guard entry-point tests (including the audit and orchestrate dispatch paths) run with the auditor seam STUBBED and assert zero live auditor invocations and no network access — the guard precondition is exercised in isolation, never by crossing into paid auditor behavior.

features.description: Explicit, audited, safe cleanup (moved from worktree-isolation-v0 F005 at its D012 split): health-gated, audit-first, no-force removal.
features.acceptance: `dontpanic plan worktree remove <plan-id>` loads the registry via the STRICT path (refusing on a corrupt registry file before touching any filesystem state) and is eligible to remove ONLY a binding that passes the canonical binding_health predicate (called from v0's module, not re-specified) AND whose worktree is fully clean — PINNED: no modified, staged, or untracked files per porcelain default mode; gitignored files are PRESERVED by default (D003 decided policy: they are still local state) — removal REFUSES when any gitignored content exists under the worktree, reporting the ignored paths explicitly, because git worktree remove would delete them; deleting ignored content is a future explicit audited cleanup command, NOT this feature; any nested .git directory under the worktree that is not a registered submodule of the repo BLOCKS removal with its path reported (it may hold work invisible to porcelain), and a REGISTERED submodule blocks removal exactly like the parent tree would: any modified, staged, untracked, or gitignored content INSIDE the submodule refuses removal with the submodule path and offending paths reported (git worktree remove can delete submodule local state, so the preserve-by-default policy applies recursively); an unhealthy binding refuses naming the predicate's failed conjunct; a dirty tree refuses printing the offending paths; eligible removal is ORDERED audit-first with TWO entries: a removal-INTENT entry (plan_id, worktree_path, branch, owner_actor, removed_by, intent timestamp) is appended and flushed BEFORE any destructive step — if that append fails the removal does not proceed (an unaudited cleanup is impossible by construction) — and a removal-OUTCOME entry recording success or the precise failure is appended AFTER the destructive steps finish (the intent entry never claims success); if the OUTCOME append itself fails after a successful removal, the command exits non-zero stating that the removal succeeded but its outcome record could not be written (the intent entry plus the absent worktree remain the durable evidence, and the registry-only completion path is unaffected because it keys on intent, never outcome); only then does it run git worktree remove WITHOUT --force and finally delete the registry binding; if the registry delete fails AFTER the worktree was removed, the command exits non-zero naming the orphaned binding (which the status model then renders as broken with its reason — never silent), and a narrowly-scoped completion path exists: re-running remove on a binding whose worktree path no longer exists AND whose audit log contains this plan's removal-INTENT entry (the worktree's absence plus recorded intent is the evidence — never a pre-recorded success claim) deletes the stale registry entry only (registry-only cleanup completing the prior removal, itself audited) — this completion path is the EXPLICIT and ONLY exception to the binding_health precondition: it requires precisely the unhealthy state missing-worktree-path PLUS the recorded removal-INTENT entry, touches nothing on the filesystem, and every other unhealthy state still refuses; the audit entry records (plan_id, worktree_path, branch, owner_actor, removed_by — the actor performing the cleanup, resolved the same way as owner_actor and recorded even when it differs — and removed_at) to a worktree audit log under $DONTPANIC_HOME; no command in this plan deletes a dirty worktree or exposes a force-removal flag (asserted by a CLI-surface test); `plan close` performs NO worktree removal — at most it prints the explicit remove command (regression test on the close path); tests cover clean removal with audit entry, the registry-delete-failure path (non-zero exit naming the orphan, then the registry-only completion re-run), the unwritable-audit-log refusal (worktree untouched), an IGNORED-CONTENT refusal fixture (a worktree that is porcelain-clean but contains gitignored files refuses removal and reports each ignored path — the central preservation case, pinned by name), dirty refusal listing files, untracked-only refusal, refusal for each unhealthy-binding conjunct, corrupt-registry refusal, and the close-does-not-remove guarantee.

features.description: Operator-local config policy across worktrees (D003): declare missing/divergent config explicitly by default; opt-in copy of a declared-safe allowlist on create; no symlinks in v1.
features.acceptance: a small declared local-config allowlist (module-level constant listing repo-root-relative, gitignored, operator-local, non-secret files — initially exactly one entry, the repo-root-relative file environments.json, pinned verbatim as a module constant so tests and implementation cannot diverge) drives explicit divergence reporting:  checks each allowlisted file and PRINTS an explicit notice for every one that exists in repo_root but not in the new worktree (declare-missing) AND, by DEFAULT with no flag, also detects and reports any allowlisted file already present in the worktree whose content DIFFERS from repo_root's copy (declare-divergent) — never silent divergence in either direction — naming the file and the copy affordance; an opt-in copy_flag (the CLI option spelled dash-dash-copy-local-config) copies ONLY allowlisted files from repo_root into the worktree at create time, reporting each copy, and REFUSES to overwrite a file that already exists in the worktree with different content (divergence is reported, never silently resolved); NO symlinks are created under any code path in this feature, and the rule is deterministic at both ends: an allowlisted SOURCE that is itself a symlink is never copied (only regular files are; the symlinked source is reported and skipped), and a preexisting TARGET path that is a symlink is treated as divergent — reported by default and REFUSED at copy time, never followed, dereferenced, or overwritten (asserted by tests for both ends plus the no-symlinked-entries assertion on the created worktree); files NOT on the allowlist are never copied even if gitignored-local; tests cover the missing-config notice, the DEFAULT divergent-content report (no flag), the opt-in copy, the copy-time divergent-content refusal, the not-on-allowlist exclusion, and the no-symlink assertion, all on temp git repos with no network.
